# HEVC range-extension and bit-depth boundaries — 16 September 2026

**AI disclosure:** This document, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the contributor's request.

This is the research decision for
[issue #28](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/28)
(parent [#12](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/12)).
It records, for every HEVC profile, bit depth and chroma format a VA client can
request, whether the driver supports it with evidence, refuses it with a
reason, or has not tested it and what that depends on. It advertises **no new
profile**, changes **no support-matrix row** and asserts **no hardware result**
beyond the pinned r11 record. Closing #28 on this document does not make any
range-extension format supported.

The one code change is a userspace boundary check: a picture that does not fit
the negotiated Main or Main10 4:2:0 contract is refused before any V4L2 control
is built from it. The check is exercised offline by `tests/hevc-capability.c`.

## What the driver negotiates today

- `hevc_profiles[]` lists `VAProfileHEVCMain` and `VAProfileHEVCMain10` only.
  `v4l2r_QueryConfigProfiles()`/`v4l2r_QueryConfigEntrypoints()` therefore
  never return a range-extension or SCC profile, and `v4l2r_CreateConfig()`
  fails them with `VA_STATUS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE`.
- Main negotiates `VA_RT_FORMAT_YUV420` and 8-bit CAPTURE buffers (NV12 or a
  tiled 8-bit layout); Main10 negotiates `VA_RT_FORMAT_YUV420_10` and 10-bit
  buffers (P010 or a tiled 10-bit layout). Any other RT format attribute is
  refused with `VA_STATUS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_RT_FORMAT`. Main10 is offered only
  when a decoder passed the P010 SPS probe (`hevc_10bit`).
- `format_infos[]` has an 8-bit 4:2:2 entry (NV16) and a 10-bit 4:2:2 entry
  (NV20), but neither has a VA FOURCC, so neither can be exported or read back
  through `vaDeriveImage`/`vaExportSurfaceHandle`. libva 2.20 also has no
  `VA_FOURCC_NV16`; a 4:2:2 image contract would need YUY2/422H-style
  conversion or a new mapping. There is no 12-bit entry at all.
- Before this change `hevc_fill_sps_pps()` copied the client's depth and
  chroma fields into `struct v4l2_ctrl_hevc_sps` unchecked. Whether a
  12-bit, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, monochrome or unequal-depth picture was refused
  depended entirely on the kernel.

## Inventory and decisions

"Unsupported" means the driver now refuses the request in userspace, with the
reason. "Untested" means nothing refuses it in principle but no qualifying VA
result exists, and names the dependency that must land first. No row is
promoted by this document.

### Ownership

- **Kernel/backend (companion repository, exact patch revisions):** whether a
  depth/chroma combination has a decoded format at all; the firmware fault on
  unequal depths; P210, 4:4:4, monochrome grey-fill and any RExt tool fields.
  Nothing in this document proposes a kernel change.
- **This driver:** which profiles and RT formats are advertised; refusing
  pictures outside the negotiated contract before submission; the image and
  export layout for each format it does advertise.
- **Client/corpus:** profile selection from `general_profile_idc`, and the
  licensing/acquisition status of any RExt vectors ([CORPUS.md](CORPUS.md)).

## Enforced boundary

`hevc_check_picture_format()` in `src/codec_hevc.c` runs on every
`VAPictureParameterBufferType` buffer, after the size check and before the
picture is staged:

1. `chroma_format_idc` must be 1 and `separate_colour_plane_flag` clear.
2. Luma and chroma bit depth must be equal.
3. The depth must be 8 or 10, the only depths with a CAPTURE layout in
   `format_infos[]`.
4. The depth must not exceed the context's negotiated depth (8 for Main,
   10 for Main10).

A refused picture returns `VA_STATUS_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_RT_FORMAT`, stages
nothing (the previous SPS is left untouched), marks the picture failed so later
slice buffers and `vaEndPicture` return `VA_STATUS_ERROR_INVALID_BUFFER`, and
emits one rate-limited `unsupported` diagnostic with `op` `hevc-picture-format`
(see [DIAGNOSTICS.md](DIAGNOSTICS.md)). The next `vaBeginPicture` starts clean.
No ioctl is issued for a refused picture; `tests/hevc-capability.c` wraps
`ioctl()` and asserts it is never reached.

What the check deliberately does **not** do:

- It does not reject 8-bit pictures in a Main10 context (see the inventory).
- It does not inspect PCM sample depths, which the kernel already normalises.
- It does not add profile entries, RT formats or any output contract.
- It is not a substitute for the companion kernel checks, which remain the
  last line of defence for clients that bypass VA-API.

### Effect on existing results

The r11 HEVC pass set is 4:2:0 at equal 8- or 10-bit depth throughout; every
one of the 144 passing vectors satisfies the four rules, so their control
contents are unchanged. `TSUNEQBD_A_MAIN10_Technicolor_2` now fails at
`vaRenderPicture` in userspace instead of at `VIDIOC_S_EXT_CTRLS` in the kernel;
it stays `expected_rejection`, not a pass. This is a source-level argument plus
the offline suite; the hardware confirmation that the exact 144-vector pass set
is preserved is listed under "Not run" in the PR and must be done through the
guard before the ticket closes.

## Offline evidence

`meson test` case `hevc-capability-profiles`: with a fake decoder that exposes
`V4L2_PIX_FMT_HEVC_SLICE` and passes the 10-bit probe, only Main, Main10 and the
VPP placeholder are enumerated; every libva HEVC range-extension and SCC profile
reports zero entrypoints and fails `vaCreateConfig` with
`UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE`; Main and Main10 refuse every RT format but their own
4:2:0 one with `UNSUPPORTED_RT_FORMAT` and leak no config handle; an 8-bit-only
decoder drops Main10 and still exposes nothing else.

`hevc-capability-picture`: 8-bit 4:2:0 under Main, 10-bit and 8-bit 4:2:0 under
Main10 are staged with the expected SPS depths. Refused, with no SPS change, a
poisoned picture and a clean next picture: five unequal-depth pairings
including the TSUNEQBD 10/9 case, equal 9-bit under Main and Main10 and equal
11-bit under Main10, 10-bit under Main, 12-bit and 16-bit under Main10,
monochrome, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 at 8/10/12 bits, separate colour planes, and an
unequal-depth picture following an accepted one in the same context. A short
picture buffer is still `INVALID_BUFFER`. Every case runs once as an AVD
context and once as a generic V4L2 context with identical results, because
the boundary is a driver contract rather than a backend quirk. `ioctl()` is
never called.

Both cases run under ASan/UBSan in CI. The twenty `hevc-picture-format`
records the picture case emits with `LIBVA_V4L2_DIAG=json` were checked with
`check_record()` from `tests/diag-schema.py` against
`tests/fixtures/diagnostics/schema.json`; the category is the existing
`unsupported`, so no schema or documentation list changes.

## Proposed implementation child

Exactly one combination has a backend decoded format and a plausible driver
path, so exactly one child is proposed, opened as
[#74](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/74); it is
not a promise of support and it stays blocked until its dependencies land:

**Qualify HEVC 8-bit 4:2:2 (`VAProfileHEVCMain422_10` at 8 bits) through
VA-API on AVD.** Scope: advertise the profile only when the decoder enumerates
NV16 for `HEVC_SLICE`; negotiate `VA_RT_FORMAT_YUV422`; select an NV16 CAPTURE
format without falling back to NV12; define the 4:2:2 image and dma-buf export
contract; keep 10-bit 4:2:2 refused (no P210); add offline negotiation and
picture tests; run the Fluster `JCT-VC-RExt` 8-bit 4:2:2 vectors under the
guard with independent reference frames once their terms are established.
Blocked by [#26](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/26)
(H.264 4:2:2 shares the NV16 contract) and
[#40](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/40) (surface
contracts across backends). `needs:hardware`, P2, M4.

Every other row is unsupported for a kernel-side reason and gets no child here;
the companion repository owns those dependencies.

## Not done and limits

- No hardware was used. The TSUNEQBD firmware fault was not replayed, and the
  144-vector HEVC pass set was not re-run on a device after this change.
- No RExt, SCC or MV-HEVC vector was acquired; C is listed as a future input
  only.
- The Asahi source A is the current upstream revision, not proven to be the
  module loaded for r11; the r11 module carried the companion patches P at
  the revision recorded in R.
- libva versions older than 2.2 lack the range-extension enums; the profile
  test compiles those checks out and still verifies Main/Main10.
